name: Tattoo Removal
summary: Ink colour, depth and skin tone all affect how removal works.
leadAnswer: Tattoo removal is the gradual fading of tattoo ink using laser energy that breaks pigment into smaller particles the body may clear over time.
seoTitle: Laser Tattoo Removal Assessment in Malaysia | Kaiteki
seoDescription: Ink type, colour, depth and skin type affect tattoo removal suitability and session count. A doctor assesses your tattoo. Book a free consultation today.

banner.alt: Illustrative photograph: a tattooed forearm resting on a clinic treatment surface

facts.label: Ink is cleared gradually by the body between visits, over a series of appointments.
Black and dark blue behave predictably; some colours and cosmetic pigments do not.
Ink composition is rarely known, so the tattoo is examined rather than described.

sections.heading: What is laser tattoo removal?
body: Laser tattoo removal uses focused laser energy to break the ink held in the skin into fragments small enough for the body's own immune system to carry away. That is why the interval between sessions matters as much as the sessions themselves.

drivers.heading: What affects your session count
drivers.intro: The tattoo is reviewed at each visit and the plan adjusted as it fades. What moves the count most:

items.body: professional tattoos place ink deeper and more densely than amateur ones. Deeper ink takes more sessions to reach and clear, and layered or covered-up work can hold several depths at once.
a larger or heavily saturated piece simply contains more pigment.

items.lead: Where it sits on the body:
items.body: areas with stronger circulation clear fragments more readily than the hands, ankles and feet (see below).

items.lead: Age of the tattoo and your own health:
items.body: older tattoos have usually faded somewhat already. Smoking, poor circulation and anything that suppresses immune function slow the clearance the treatment depends on.

variant.heading: How different inks respond
variant.intro: Ink composition is not standardised and is rarely documented, so this describes general behaviour rather than what your tattoo will do.

locationBlock.heading: Where the tattoo sits
locationBlock.intro: The body clears ink fragments through the lymphatic system, so how well an area drains changes how a tattoo behaves between sessions.

cards.title: Upper arm, chest and back
cards.body: Strong circulation and good lymphatic drainage.

cards.title: Hands, fingers, ankles and feet
cards.body: Slower drainage and thinner skin over bone. These typically need longer intervals and more patience, and they are the areas where expectations most often need adjusting.

cards.title: Face, neck and eyebrows
cards.body: Treated with particular caution. Cosmetic pigment is unpredictable, the skin is thin, and any pigment change here is highly visible.

note.title: Over a scar or a raised tattoo?
note.body: Tattoos placed over scar tissue, or work that sits raised or itchy, are assessed separately. So is any tattoo containing a mole or a changing mark, which must be examined before laser is used anywhere near it.

seeDoctor.heading: What a doctor checks first
seeDoctor.intro: Before any laser is used, an assessment covers a short list of things that change whether treatment is appropriate at all:
triggers: The colours present, and whether the clinic's platform has a wavelength for each of them.
Whether the tattoo is a cover-up, a rework, or has been treated elsewhere before.
Your medical history, including anything affecting immune function, healing or photosensitivity.

ctaMid.heading: Wondering if yours can be treated?
ctaMid.body: Send us a photo on WhatsApp and a doctor can tell you what to expect from an assessment.

treatmentsIntro: Tattoo removal at our clinics is a single treatment carried out over a course of appointments.

pico-laser.why: For breaking ink into particles the body clears
pico-laser.body: A picosecond laser delivers energy in pulses short enough to shatter pigment mechanically rather than by heating it, which reduces the heat delivered to surrounding skin.

firstVisit.intro: The tattoo itself is examined: ink composition is rarely known, so it cannot be judged from a description.

steps.title: History
steps.body: When the tattoo was done, whether it is a cover-up or has been treated before, and how your skin usually heals.

steps.title: Examination
steps.body: Colours, density, depth and the surrounding skin.

steps.title: Discussion
steps.body: Which colours are likely to respond, and how sessions are spaced.

steps.title: Test patch and plan
steps.body: Where colour behaviour is uncertain, a small test area is treated first, then a sequence and a review point.

items.body: Immediate whitening of the treated area, then redness, swelling, tenderness and often blistering or crusting over the following days. The area may weep briefly.
Medium and deeper skin tones carry a higher chance of hypopigmentation, where treated skin ends up lighter than the surrounding area, and of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.

Scarring is uncommon but possible, particularly if crusts are picked or if sessions are spaced too closely. Some pigments, notably white and flesh-tone cosmetic ink, can darken on contact with laser energy.

Complete clearance cannot be promised for any tattoo. Yellow and pastel inks often persist after everything else has gone, and a faint shadow or a change in skin texture where the tattoo was is a common end point. Removal does not restore the skin to how it looked before the tattoo.

risks.disclose: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, take photosensitising medication or oral acne medication, have a history of keloid scarring or cold sores, have a condition affecting immune function or healing, have tanned recently, or have had the tattoo treated anywhere else before.

costFactors.intro: Pricing is set once the tattoo is assessed. It depends on:
factors: The size of the piece, and how densely the ink is packed within it.
How many colours are present, since some need a different wavelength from the rest.
Where it sits on the body, which affects both technique and how the area is expected to clear.
How many sessions, which is reviewed at each visit rather than fixed in advance.
Whether a test patch is carried out first, which is standard for colours and cosmetic pigment.

technologyIntro: Different ink colours absorb different wavelengths, so a platform with only one wavelength can only reach some of a tattoo.

faqs.q: Can a tattoo be completely removed?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but it cannot be promised for any tattoo before it has been treated. Black and dark blue generally clear most predictably, while yellow, pastel and some cosmetic pigments often persist after everything else has gone.

faqs.q: How many sessions will it take?
faqs.a: There is no fixed number. It depends on the colours, how deeply and densely the ink was placed, the size, where it sits on the body, your skin tone and how well you heal.

It is generally described as more uncomfortable than getting the tattoo, though it is over far more quickly. People often compare it to a hot elastic band snapping against the skin. Numbing cream is applied beforehand and cooling is used during and after.

faqs.q: Is it safe on darker skin?
faqs.a: Yes, with the right wavelength, conservative settings and longer intervals. The specific issue is that melanin in the skin competes with the ink for laser energy, which raises the chance of the treated area ending up lighter or darker than the surrounding skin.

faqs.q: Can eyebrow or lip tattoos be removed?
faqs.a: They can be assessed, but they are among the least predictable pigments to treat. A test patch on a small, discreet area is standard practice before treating anything on the face, and the assessment may conclude that treatment is not advisable.

faqs.q: What do I need to do afterwards?
faqs.a: Keep the area clean, dry and covered as instructed, do not pick at blisters or crusts, avoid swimming pools, saunas and heavy exercise until it has settled, and keep it out of the sun completely. Sun exposure on treated skin is the most common cause of pigment change afterwards.

relatedConcerns.reason: Pigment change after removal is assessed the same way as any other.
Pigmented marks are treated with related laser principles.
Texture change left behind is assessed alongside scarring of any origin.
